Lemma 6.78 (The first character contributes the class number). Let E be CM, O the coefficient DVR, and D = K/O with trivial G_{E}-action. The group of continuous classes in H^{1}(E, D) unramified at every finite place has normalized length v_{ℓ}(h_{E}). Every submodule of such classes has finite normalized length at most this number.

Proof. For trivial action, a continuous cocycle is a continuous homomorphism G_{E} → (D, +) and all coboundaries are zero. Unramifiedness says precisely that the homomorphism kills each finite inertia sub-group. It factors through the maximal unramified abelian extension. The Hilbert class field theorem identifies this finite quotient with the ideal class group Cl(E). We use the theorem in J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, version 4.03 (2020), Theorem 0.4 and the Hilbert-class-field conclusion immediately following it, page 4; equivalently Chapter V, Example 3.9, page 159. Its condition at real places adds nothing here, since E has no real places. Thus the group in question is

Hom(Cl(E), D).

Only the ℓ-primary part of the finite class group contributes. Write that part as ⊕_{i}ℤ/ℓ^{ai}. Evaluation at the cyclic generators identifies its Hom module with ⊕_{i}D[ℓ^{ai}] as an O-module. The map O/ℓ^{ai}O →∑D[ℓ^{ai}] sending b to b/ℓ^{ai}+ O is an isomorphism. Its length is e_{O}a_{i}. The total length is consequently e_{Oi}a_{i} = e_{O}v_{ℓ}(h_{E}). Division by e_{O} gives the displayed normalized value. Length monotonicity gives the assertion for any submodule.

In the first character block the twist makes the action trivial, as used in Lemma 6.5. If its strict local conditions vanish on every finite inertia group, this lemma supplies exactly the class-group term in the comparison. For the higher characters, the analogous strict group is the specified Tate-twist Selmer group defining Sha_{ℓ}(c −1); the remaining task is to verify that the local conditions used to define that group are the same ones as those imposed by the row and column construction. The class-field estimate itself requires no assumption about the growth of class numbers.

The nonnumerical content at this point is the simultaneous existence of the comparison data just used. At ℓ= 2, the host condition 4 | Q_{S} supplies the required cyclotomic level, and s_{0} = v_{2}(Q_{S}) = s. At ℓ= 3 outside the small set, the hypotheses 3 ̸= q, d give v_{3}(N) = v_{3}(Q_{S}) = 0, so s_{0} = s = 1. The host splitting condition at small primes, its splitting bound at least 60, and the exclusion of the two auxiliary primes are used to choose the conjugate row–column declaration. The crystalline comparison, nonzero Hodge–Tate jumps and integral lifting theorem then have to supply the three quantities e, c_{0}, b_{0} and the invariant bounds in Lemma 6.82. A proof of this existence statement cannot be replaced by the calculation of its constants.

The transfer from the local crystalline statements to these constants has the following explicit content. It is useful to distinguish the transfer from the local crystalline statements themselves.

Lemma 6.83 (Descent of an integral finite-condition lift). Let F^{′}/F be finite Galois, and let L_{1} →L_{2} be a morphism of integral crystalline lattices. Suppose restriction and corestriction preserve their finite local conditions and commute with this morphism. If every finite class over F^{′} becomes a lifted finite class after multiplication by ℓ^{a}, then every finite class over F does so after multiplication by ℓ^{a+vℓ([F ′:F])}.

Proof. For a finite class z over F, lift ℓ^{a} res(z) over F^{′} and corestrict its lift. Naturality shows that its image is ℓ^{a} cor res(z) = ℓ^{a}[F^{′} : F]z. Write [F^{′} : F] = ℓ^{b}u with u prime to ℓ. Multiplication by u^{−1} ∈ ℤ^{×}_{ℓ} preserves the integral finite condition and the image of the lattice morphism. Applying it gives a lift of ℓ^{a+b}z, as required. The same proof on finite cocycles is modulo the integral coboundaries, which is exactly the lifting convention used here.

For the source’s cyclotomic local fields, write

L_{1} = s + ⌊log_{ℓ}(2h)⌋+ ⌊log_{ℓ}N⌋+ 1.

The comparison first passes from a subfield of ℚ_{ℓ}(µ_{lcm(ℓ,N)}) to that full cyclotomic field. Its index has ℓ-valuation at most ⌊log_{ℓ}N⌋+1: the full cyclotomic degree is at most φ(lcm(ℓ, N)) ≤ℓN, the relative index divides it, and v_{ℓ}(a) ≤⌊log_{ℓ}a⌋ for positive a. The local lifting estimate at the full field is at most 32(2hs+1). Consequently Lemma 6.83 gives the asserted e = 32(2hs+1)+L_{1}, since L_{1} is at least this index correction. The local lifting estimate used in this deduction is proved in Proposition 6.63 for the actual cyclotomic period modules. Restriction preserves the finite condition by restricting its period coboundary; corestriction does so by summing the conjugate period coboundaries over the finite set of coset representatives. The selected setup must still identify its local lattices and class maps with these actual realizations.

Proof. The integer logarithm bound 2h < ℓ^{⌊logℓ(2h)⌋+1} gives M ≤ 2s + ⌊log_{ℓ}(2h)⌋+ 2 ≤ 2L_{1}. For 0 ≤ i < k ≤ h + 1 and u ∈ U, u ̸= i, the nonzero integer u −i has absolute value at most 2h. Thus v_{ℓ}(u −i) ≤⌊log_{ℓ}(2h)⌋. The sharper bound M + ⌊log_{ℓ}(2h)⌋≤2L_{1} from the first display therefore gives r_{U}(i) ≤2nL_{1}. Since L_{1} ≥1, 2 + max(1, r_{U}(i)) ≤3(n + 1)L_{1}. There are k summands, proving the first bound; its case k = 1 is at most (3n + 5)L_{1} ≤20(n + 1)L_{1}.

For the last inequality use that bound with k = e + 1 ≤ t. Also v_{ℓ}(e) ≤ e, v_{ℓ}(e + 1) ≤ e + 1, ⌊e/(ℓ−1)⌋≤ e, s ≤ L_{1}, and g ≤ L_{1}. After replacing e + 1 by t all these summands are bounded by 14(t + 1)(n + 1)L_{1}, which is at most the displayed 40(t + 1)(n + 1)L_{1}. For example, the five groups 2L_{1}, 3t(n + 1)L_{1}, (e + 3)s, the three valuation/division terms, and 1 + g are bounded respectively by 2, 3, 3, 3, 2 times (t + 1)(n + 1)L_{1}; their total is at most 13 times that quantity. This supplies the claimed weaker bound with room to spare.

Thus the source’s invariant-annihilator theorem with exponent B_{1} gives c_{0} = 20(n + 1)L_{1}, and its trivial-block theorem with the last exponent gives b_{0} = 40(t + 1)(n + 1)L_{1}. A G_{F} -invariant vector remains invariant after restriction, so the invariant-annihilator deduction incurs no index correction. For the finite-condition cocycle the index correction is supplied by Lemma 6.83. These deductions explain the exact formulas in Lemma 6.82. The local finite-condition lifting theorem (Proposition 6.63), the quantitative invariant annihilator with exponent c_{0} = 20(n + 1)L_{1} (Corollary 6.70), and the quantitative trivial-block annihilator and twist-quotient length bound with exponent b_{0} = 40(t + 1)(n + 1)L_{1} (Corollary 6.77) are all proved above. The simultaneous realization and identification of these local lattices, Wach data, and row quotients within every compatible family setup SetupAlt are proved in Subsection 6.7 (Theorem 6.103).
